passages.note: Bill overview lists him as a co-sponsor of the single-subject athletics bill; the page prints no operative text.
House Third Reading (final passage) roll call shows his Aye on a divided 31-24 vote, so it is not near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex.
passages.note: Enacted text of the instrument he co-sponsored and voted for; it names no voter, so actor and tally are null here.

rows.reasoning: Nguyen co-sponsored SB1165 (2022) and voted Y on House Third Reading, a single-subject bill whose operative section designates teams by biological sex and provides that teams designated for "females", "women" or "girls" "may not be open to students of the male sex" — the rung that would "require transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth." The rung that would "completely ban all transgender athletes from competing in any organized sports competitions" is excluded by the bill's own text, which "does not restrict the eligibility of any student to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated as being for "males", "men" or "boys" or designated as "coed" or "mixed"."
